item.description: Divide recipe cost by your target food cost percentage. Worked example, common mistakes, and a weekly checklist for small operators.

item.description: Restaurant labor cost percentage with benefits: the formula, the NRA medians (34.2% and 36.5%), a worked example and a checklist for this week.

item.description: Calculate latte pricing from recipe cost and target margin. Includes real cost breakdown, markup formula, and 4 fixes for low-margin drinks.

item.description: Calculate turnover cost: headcount × rate × $2,706 per departure. Full-service restaurants lose ~92% of hourly staff yearly (Black Box Intelligence 2025). Track it monthly.

item.description: Learn the break-even formula for restaurants, see a worked example in covers per day, and understand how fixed costs and margin drive your threshold.

item.description: Learn the beverage cost formula, see a worked example, and compare your pour cost to industry benchmarks for bars and restaurants.

item.description: Industry benchmarks for prime cost percentage by segment: full-service, bar, and cafe. Learn the target range and how to improve it.

item.title: What Should Labor Cost Be for a Bar? (Benchmarks + How to Calculate)
item.description: Bar labor cost should be 25 to 35% of sales. Learn how to calculate yours, what to include, and when your percentage is too high.

item.title: How to Calculate Prime Cost for a Restaurant (Formula + Example)
item.description: Prime cost = COGS + total labor. Learn the formula, see a worked example, and download a free calculator to track yours monthly.

item.description: Step-by-step guide to calculate restaurant food cost percentage using beginning inventory, purchases, and ending inventory.
